subject.title: Feature Request: Abstract file scanning pipeline as Memory Plugin API

question: Should OpenClaw add a public host-delivered memory file-ingestion API for active memory plugins, and what local-file trust boundary should govern files sent to third-party plugin code?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent SDK shape and the security policy for exposing local memory and extraPath file contents require maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve Narrow SDK Design First
options.body: Design a minimal ingestion capability with explicit security, compatibility, and test requirements before implementation.

options.title: Keep Scanning Plugin-Owned
options.body: Document that memory plugins may use current list/read helpers but must own watchers, indexing, deletion, and cleanup behavior themselves.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Memory Backend Contract
options.body: Defer this until a broader memory backend contract decides file ingestion, search, get, writeback, and status ownership together.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow SDK Design First
recommendation.body: Design a minimal ingestion capability with explicit security, compatibility, and test requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the memory-host SDK extraction and memory plugin-boundary design that this decision would extend.
